workload: 8000 torrent names (4/5 long ASCII release names, 1/5 CJK titles), each cropped to widths 24, 40, 64 and 80 with an ellipsis tail, repeated 4 times.
notes: strcrop wcswidth-scans the whole name, builds a wide-character index via list.pop(0), then wcswidth-scans the joined prefix again. Printable ASCII (typical release names) has display width equal to len, so a slice matches current output and skips both scans; wide names stay on the existing walk. On this mix that is several times faster, and on ASCII-only names far faster, with identical crops.

workload: 30000 integer byte counts passed through convert.size and convert.bandwidth with unit='byte', repeated 6 times, as SizeInBytes and BandwidthInBytes do when polled rate and size fields are rebuilt.
notes: DataSizeConverter.__call__ builds an Int to attach the unit, then a second Int that converts to the same unit. SizeInBytes and BandwidthInBytes take this path on every cache miss. Returning one Int when the value is already a plain number in the target unit keeps the converter tests' results and removes about half of the constructions.

workload: 16000 offline torrent dicts filtered with TorrentFilter('active|!complete'), the default first tab in stig/settings/defaults.py.
notes: FilterChain.apply builds nested any()/all() generators for every torrent on every refresh. A straight-line predicate in apply() yields the same objects and drops those temporary generators. Counted with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc so each object allocation is a malloc; 7 runs were identical.
